newsitem.title: UK: Man raises forecast for E. Europe sugar production.
newsitem.headline: Man raises forecast for E. Europe sugar production.

text.p: East European sugar output should total 8.5 million tonnes white value for the 1996/97 crop year, just over 400,000 tonnes lower than last season, E D & F Man said on Tuesday.
"Although the overall East European estimates are still below last year, in some areas production figures have crept up," Man said in its latest monthly report.
In its last estimate, Man forecast total sugar production for the region at 8.2 million tonnes, after 8.9 million in 1995/96.
Man estimated sugar output in Poland, the region's third largest producer, at 2.2 million tonnes. It gave no comparative figure.
Romania, one of the smaller producers, was expecting this year's final sugar outturn at 220,000 tonnes following good autumn weather which limited expected crop losses, Man said.
